Abstract.

We establish basic properties of a sheaf of graded algebras canonically associated to every relative affine scheme f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S endowed with an action of the additive group scheme 𝔾a,S\mathbb{G}_{a,S} over a base scheme or algebraic space SS, which we call the (relative) Rees algebra of the 𝔾a,S\mathbb{G}_{a,S}-action. We illustrate these properties on several examples which played important roles in the development of the algebraic theory of locally nilpotent derivations and give some applications to the construction of families of affine threefolds with 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions.

2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
14R20; 14R25; 14L30; 13A30

Introduction

The study of regular actions of the additive group 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} on affine varieties has led to an increased understanding of both algebraic and geometric properties of these varieties. A 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on an affine variety XX defined over a field kk of characteristic zero is fully determined by its velocity vector field, which takes the form of a kk-derivation ∂\partial of the coordinate ring AA of XX with the property that AA is the increasing union of the kernels of the iterated kk-linear differential operators ∂n\partial^{n}, n≥1n\geq 1. Due to this correspondence, the study of regular 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions developed into a very rich algebraic theory of such differential operators, called locally nilpotent kk-derivations. The most fundamental object associated to such a derivation is its kernel, which coincides with the subalgebra of 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-invariant functions on XX. Kernels of locally nilpotent derivations have been intensively studied during the last decades, with many applications to the construction of new invariants to distinguish affine spaces among all affine varieties and to the understanding of automorphism groups of affine varieties close to affine spaces (see [15] and the references therein). A second natural subspace associated to a locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial of a kk-algebra AA which has been very much studied from an algebraic point of view is the kernel Ker∂2\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{2} of its square ∂2\partial^{2}. Geometrically, the elements of Ker∂2∖Ker∂\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{2}\setminus\mathrm{Ker}\partial, usually called local slices, are regular functions on X=Spec⁡(A)X=\mathrm{Spec}(A) which restrict to coordinate functions on general orbits of the corresponding 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action. The image of ∂|Ker∂2:Ker∂2→Ker∂\partial|_{\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{2}}:\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{Ker}\partial is an ideal of Ker∂\mathrm{Ker}\partial, called the plinth ideal, which encodes basic geometric properties of the algebraic quotient morphism X→X//𝔾a=Spec(Ker∂)X\rightarrow X/\!/\mathbb{G}_{a}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathrm{Ker}\partial).

A more systematic study of the algebro-geometric properties encoded by the whole increasing exhaustive filtration of AA formed by the subspaces Fn=Ker∂n+1F_{n}=\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n+1}, n≥0n\geq 0, was initiated only quite recently by Alhajjar [1, 2] and Freudenburg [14]. For instance, they observed that for an integral finitely generated kk-algebra AA endowed with a nonzero locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial, the infinite collection of inclusions Fn↪Fn+1F_{n}\hookrightarrow F_{n+1}, n≥0n\geq 0, gives rise to a collection of successive inclusions k⁡[Fn]↪k⁡[Fn+1]k[F_{n}]\hookrightarrow k[F_{n+1}] between the kk-subalgebras of AA that they generate. This sequence exhausts AA after finitely many steps, i.e. k⁡[Fr]=Ak[F_{r}]=A for some r∈ℕr\in\mathbb{N}. These inclusions correspond geometrically to a canonical sequence of birational 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-equivariant morphisms

X=Spec⁡(A)≅Spec⁡(k⁡[Fr])→Spec⁡(k⁡[Fr−1])→⋯→Spec⁡(k⁡[F1])X=\mathrm{Spec}(A)\cong\mathrm{Spec}(k[F_{r}])\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k[F_{r-1}])\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k[F_{1}])

factorizing the algebraic quotient morphism X→Spec⁡(F0)X\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(F_{0}). The basic properties of this factorization have been established by Freudenburg [14]. He described in particular an algorithm to compute, under suitable noetherianity conditions, the subspaces FnF_{n}, n≥0n\geq 0, as well as the corresponding algebras k⁡[Fn]k[F_{n}].

In this article, we shift the focus to a complementary approach which considers the properties of the two natural graded algebras that can be canonically associated to a filtered algebra: its associated graded algebra and its Rees algebra. For a kk-algebra AA with a nonzero locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial, these are thus the algebras

gr∂A=⨁n≥0Ker∂n+1/Ker∂n and R(A,∂)=⨁n≥0Ker∂n+1.\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n+1}/\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n}\quad\textrm{ and }\quad R(A,\partial)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n+1}.

The first one already plays an important role in the computation of Makar-Limanov invariants of certain affine varieties [22, 2], but to our knowledge, the second one, which we henceforth call the Rees algebra of (A,∂)(A,\partial), has not been considered before in this context. Besides the fact that these Rees algebras are functorial with respect to 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-equivariant morphisms, two basic properties which motivate their study are the following:

∙\bullet First, the canonical graded homomorphism of degree 00

k[θ]=⨁n≥0k→⨁n≥0Ker∂n+1k[\theta]=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}k\rightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n+1}

induced by the inclusion k⊂Ker∂n+1k\subset\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{n+1} for every n≥0n\geq 0 provides a one-parameter deformation

π:Spec(R(A,∂))→𝔸k1=Spec(k[θ])\pi:\mathrm{Spec}(R(A,\partial))\rightarrow\mathbb{A}_{k}^{1}=\mathrm{Spec}(k[\theta])

whose fibers over the points 00 and 11 are canonically isomorphic to Spec⁡(gr∂​A)\mathrm{Spec}(\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A) and Spec⁡(A)\mathrm{Spec}(A) respectively.

∙\bullet Second, the Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) carries canonical extensions of ∂\partial to homogeneous locally nilpotent k⁡[θ]k[\theta]-derivations of homogeneous degree mm for every m≥−1m\geq-1, whose corresponding 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions on Spec(R(A,∂))\mathrm{Spec}(R(A,\partial)) make π\pi a 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-equivariant deformation of Spec⁡(A)\mathrm{Spec}(A) endowed with the 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action defined by ∂\partial. For m=−1m=-1, the induced 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on the fiber π−1​(0)\pi^{-1}(0) coincides with the one which is defined by the homogeneous kk-derivation gr∂\mathrm{gr}\partial of gr∂​A\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A of degree −1-1, the latter derivation being canonically associated to ∂\partial. On the other hand, for m=0m=0 the 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on Spec(R(A,∂))\mathrm{Spec}(R(A,\partial)) descends to a 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on Proj(R(A,∂))\mathrm{Proj}(R(A,\partial)) and we obtain in particular a canonical 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-equivariant open embedding Spec(A)↪Proj(R(A,∂))\mathrm{Spec}(A)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Proj}(R(A,\partial)) which provides a canonical relative 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-equivariant completion of Spec⁡(A)\mathrm{Spec}(A) over Spec(Ker∂)\mathrm{Spec}(\mathrm{Ker}\partial).

Example.

The Rees algebra R⁡(k⁡[t],∂∂t)R(k[t],\frac{\partial}{\partial t}) of the additive group 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} acting on itself by translations is isomorphic to the polynomial ring in two variables k⁡[t,θ]k[t,\theta] with its standard grading, and the associated graded algebra gr∂∂t​k​[t]\mathrm{gr}_{\frac{\partial}{\partial t}}k[t] is the the polynomial ring k⁡[t]k[t] endowed with its standard grading. The locally nilpotent k⁡[θ]k[\theta]-derivation ∂∂t\frac{\partial}{\partial t} of k⁡[t,θ]k[t,\theta] is homogeneous of degree −1-1, and Spec⁡(R⁡(k⁡[t],∂∂t))\mathrm{Spec}(R(k[t],\frac{\partial}{\partial t})) endowed with the corresponding 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action is just the trivial 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-torsor over Spec⁡(k⁡[θ])\mathrm{Spec}(k[\theta]) via the projection

π=prθ:Spec⁡(R⁡(k⁡[t],∂∂t))→Spec⁡(k⁡[θ]).\pi=\mathrm{pr}_{\theta}:\mathrm{Spec}(R(k[t],\frac{\partial}{\partial t}))\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k[\theta]).

On the other hand, the locally nilpotent k⁡[θ]k[\theta]-derivation θ​∂∂t\theta\frac{\partial}{\partial t} of k⁡[t,θ]k[t,\theta] is homogeneous of degree 00 and the open immersion

𝔾a=Spec(k[t])↪ℙ1=Projk(k[t,θ]),t↦[t:1]\mathbb{G}_{a}=\mathrm{Spec}(k[t])\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(k[t,\theta]),\quad t\mapsto[t:1]

is equivariant for the 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action t′⋅[t:θ]↦[t+t′θ:θ]t^{\prime}\cdot[t:\theta]\mapsto[t+t^{\prime}\theta:\theta] on ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1} induced by θ​∂∂t\theta\frac{\partial}{\partial t}.

The content of the article is the following. In the first section we establish basic general properties of Rees algebras of additive group scheme actions in a relative and characteristic free setting. Namely, given a fixed base scheme or algebraic space SS, we consider schemes or algebraic spaces XX that are endowed with an action of the additive group scheme 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} and which admit a 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-invariant affine morphism f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S. Having this flexibility is useful even in the absolute case of an affine variety XX over a base field endowed with 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action since we can then analyze the relative structure of XX with respect to any 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-invariant morphism f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S to some scheme or algebraic space. The second section focuses on the case of algebraic varieties over a field of characteristic zero. We study the behavior of Rees algebras under certain type of equivariant morphisms and characterize geometrically those that are finitely generated. We also describe an algorithm to compute generators of these algebras. The last section is devoted to a selection of examples which illustrate the interplay between relative and absolute Rees algebras. We also present an application of Rees algebras to the construction and classification of affine extensions of 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-torsors over punctured surfaces [11, 18], a class of varieties which form one of the building blocks of the classification theory of affine threefolds with 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions.

1. Rees algebras of affine 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-schemes

Given a scheme or an algebraic space SS, we denote by 𝔾a,S=S×ℤ𝔾a,ℤ=Spec⁡(𝒪S​[t])\mathbb{G}_{a,S}=S\times_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{G}_{a,\mathbb{Z}}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]) the additive group scheme over SS. We denote by m:𝔾a,S×S𝔾a,S→𝔾a,Sm:\mathbb{G}_{a,S}\times_{S}\mathbb{G}_{a,S}\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{a,S} and e:S→𝔾a,Se:S\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{a,S} its group law and neutral section respectively. By an affine SS-scheme f:X→Sf:X\rightarrow S, we mean the relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent sheaf 𝒜=f∗​𝒪X\mathcal{A}=f_{*}\mathcal{O}_{X} of 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebras. We say that XX is of finite type over SS if 𝒜\mathcal{A} is locally of finite type as an 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra.

1.1. Additive group scheme actions on relative affine schemes

Let SS be a scheme or an algebraic space. An action μ:𝔾a,S×SX→X\mu:\mathbb{G}_{a,S}\times_{S}X\rightarrow X of 𝔾a,S\mathbb{G}_{a,S} on an affine SS-scheme f:X=SpecS​(𝒜)→Sf:X=\mathrm{Spec}_{S}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow S is equivalently determined by its 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra co-morphism

μ∗:𝒜→𝒜⊗𝒪S𝒪S​[t]=𝒜⁡[t],\mu^{*}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]=\mathcal{A}[t],

which satisfies the usual axioms of a group co-action, namely the commutativity of the following two diagrams:

(1.1)

For every i≥0i\geq 0, let pi:𝒪S​[t]=⨁j=0∞𝒪S→𝒪S\mathrm{p}_{i}:\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]=\bigoplus_{j=0}^{\infty}\mathcal{O}_{S}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{S} be the projection onto the ii-th factor, and let D(i)=(id𝒜⊗pi)∘μ∗:𝒜→𝒜D^{(i)}=(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}}\otimes\mathrm{p}_{i})\circ\mu^{*}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}. The following lemma is a well-known consequence of the commutativity of the above diagrams.

Lemma 1.

The 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-module endomorphisms D(i)=(id𝒜⊗pi)∘μ∗:𝒜→𝒜D^{(i)}=(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}}\otimes\mathrm{p}_{i})\circ\mu^{*}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A} are differential operators of order ≤i\leq i which satisfy the following properties:

  1. (1)

    The operator D(0)D^{(0)} is the identity map of 𝒜\mathcal{A},

  2. (2)

    For every i≥0i\geq 0, the Leibniz rule D(i)​(a​b)=∑j=0iD(j)​(a)​D(i−j)​(b)D^{(i)}(ab)=\sum_{j=0}^{i}D^{(j)}(a)D^{(i-j)}(b) holds for every pair of local sections a,ba,b of 𝒜\mathcal{A} over SS,

  3. (3)

    For every i,j≥0i,j\geq 0, D(i)∘D(j)=(i+ji)​D(i+j)D^{(i)}\circ D^{(j)}=\binom{i+j}{i}D^{(i+j)},

  4. (4)

    We have 𝒜=⋃n≥0(⋂i>n𝒦​e​r​D(i))\mathcal{A}=\bigcup_{n\geq 0}(\bigcap_{i>n}\mathcal{K}erD^{(i)}).

Proof.

The fact that D(0)=id𝒜D^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}} follows from the commutativity of the diagram on the right in (1.1). Given local sections a,ba,b of 𝒜\mathcal{A} over SS, the fact that μ∗\mu^{*} is a 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra homomorphism implies that μ∗​(a​b)=μ∗​(a)​μ∗​(b)\mu^{*}(ab)=\mu^{*}(a)\mu^{*}(b). Writing μ∗​(a)=∑i≥0D(i)​(a)​ti\mu^{*}(a)=\sum_{i\geq 0}D^{(i)}(a)t^{i}, μ∗​(b)=∑i≥0D(i)​(b)​ti\mu^{*}(b)=\sum_{i\geq 0}D^{(i)}(b)t^{i} and μ∗​(a​b)=∑i≥0D(i)​(a​b)​ti\mu^{*}(ab)=\sum_{i\geq 0}D^{(i)}(ab)t^{i}, we have

D(i)​(a​b)=∑j=0iD(j)​(a)​D(i−j)​(b)D^{(i)}(ab)=\sum_{j=0}^{i}D^{(j)}(a)D^{(i-j)}(b)

for every i≥0i\geq 0, which proves Property (2). Let aa be a local section of 𝒜\mathcal{A} over SS and write μ∗​(a)=∑i≥0D(i)​(a)​ti\mu^{*}(a)=\sum_{i\geq 0}D^{(i)}(a)t^{i} and for every i≥0i\geq 0, μ∗​(D(i)​(a))=∑j≥0D(j)​(D(i)​(a))​vj\mu^{*}(D^{(i)}(a))=\sum_{j\geq 0}D^{(j)}(D^{(i)}(a))v^{j}. The commutativity of the diagram on the left in (1.1) implies that

∑i≥0D(i)​(a)​(t+v)i=∑i≥0(∑j≥0D(j)​(D(i)​(a))​vj)​ti,\sum_{i\geq 0}D^{(i)}(a)(t+v)^{i}=\sum_{i\geq 0}(\sum_{j\geq 0}D^{(j)}(D^{(i)}(a))v^{j})t^{i},

from which it follows, by identifying the terms in ti​vjt^{i}v^{j}, that D(j)​(D(i)​(a))=(i+ji)​D(i+j)​(a)D^{(j)}(D^{(i)}(a))=\binom{i+j}{i}D^{(i+j)}(a). This proves Property (3). For every n≥0n\geq 0, ℱn=⋂i>n𝒦​e​r​D(i)\mathcal{F}_{n}=\bigcap_{i>n}\mathcal{K}erD^{(i)} is an 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-submodule of 𝒜\mathcal{A} which is equal to the inverse image by μ∗\mu^{*} of the 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-submodule 𝒜⊗𝒪S𝒪S​[t]≤n\mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]_{\leq n} of 𝒜⊗𝒪S𝒪S​[t]\mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]. The union ⋃n≥0ℱn\bigcup_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{F}_{n} is an 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-submodule of 𝒜\mathcal{A} which is stable under multiplication by Property (2), hence an 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-subalgebra of 𝒜\mathcal{A}. The fact that the inclusion ⋃n≥0ℱn↪𝒜\bigcup_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{F}_{n}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{A} is an isomorphism of 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebras is then checked on an open cover of SS by affine open subsets as in [26]. This proves Property (4). ∎

Definition 2.

A collection of 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-linear differential operators D(i):𝒜→𝒜D^{(i)}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}, i∈ℤ≥0i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} which satisfy the properties of Lemma 1 is called a locally finite iterative higher 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-derivation (𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-LFIHD for short) of the quasi-coherent 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra 𝒜\mathcal{A}.

Conversely, for every 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-LFIHD D={D(i)}i≥0D=\{D^{(i)}\}_{i\geq 0} of a quasi-coherent 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra 𝒜\mathcal{A}, the exponential map

μ∗:=exp⁡(t​D)=∑i=0∞D(i)⊗ti:𝒜→𝒜⊗𝒪S𝒪S​[t],a↦∑i=0∞D(i)​(a)⊗ti\mu^{*}:=\exp(tD)=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}D^{(i)}\otimes t^{i}:\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S}[t],\quad a\mapsto\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}D^{(i)}(a)\otimes t^{i}

is the co-morphism of a 𝔾a,S\mathbb{G}_{a,S}-action μ:𝔾a,S×SX→X\mu:\mathbb{G}_{a,S}\times_{S}X\rightarrow X on XX (see e.g. [26]).

The quasi-coherent 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-algebra 𝒜\mathcal{A} of an affine SS-scheme f:X=SpecS​(𝒜)→Sf:X=\mathrm{Spec}_{S}(\mathcal{A})\rightarrow S equipped with a 𝔾a,S\mathbb{G}_{a,S}-action is endowed with an increasing exhaustive filtration by its 𝒪S\mathcal{O}_{S}-submodules

ℱn=(μ∗)−1​(𝒜⊗𝒪S𝒪S​[t]≤n)=⋂i>n𝒦​e​r​D(i),n∈ℤ≥0,\mathcal{F}_{n}=(\mu^{*})^{-1}(\mathcal{A}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{O}_{S}[t]_{\leq n})=\bigcap_{i>n}\mathcal{K}erD^{(i)},\quad n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0},

consisting of elements whose image by μ∗\mu^{*} are polynomials with coefficients in 𝒜\mathcal{A} of degree less than or equal to nn in the variable tt. The following lemma, whose proof is left to the reader, records some basic properties of this filtration.

With the above notation, the following hold:

1.2. Rees algebras and associated graded homomorphisms

Definition 4.

2. Rees algebras of affine 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-varieties over a field of characteristic zero

This section is devoted to the study of Rees algebras in the “absolute” case where the base scheme SS is the spectrum of a field kk, which we further assume to be of characteristic zero for simplicity. We establish basic additional properties of Rees algebras in this context, with a special emphasis on their behavior with respect to equivariant birational morphisms such as the normalization or equivariant affine modifications. We also study the problem of finite generation of Rees algebras from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. Throughout this section, we denote the additive group 𝔾a,k\mathbb{G}_{a,k} simply by 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}.

2.1. Basic properties of global Rees algebras of affine 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-varieties


Here S=Spec⁡(k)S=\mathrm{Spec}(k) is the spectrum of an algebraically closed field kk of characteristic zero and X=Spec⁡(A)X=\mathrm{Spec}(A) is the spectrum of an integral kk-algebra of finite type. In this context, a kk-LFIHD D={D(i)}i≥0D=\{D^{(i)}\}_{i\geq 0} of AA is uniquely determined by D(i)=1i!∂iD^{(i)}=\frac{1}{i!}\partial^{i} where ∂=D(1):A→A\partial=D^{(1)}:A\rightarrow A is a kk-derivation of AA such that A=⋃n≥0(⋂i>nKer∂i)A=\bigcup_{n\geq 0}(\bigcap_{i>n}\mathrm{Ker}\partial^{i}). 2.2. Rees algebras and equivariant birational morphisms

We now consider the behavior of Rees algebras under certain equivariant birational morphisms between affine varieties. Let (A,∂)(A,\partial) be an integral kk-algebra endowed with a non-zero locally nilpotent kk-derivation and let A′⊂Frac⁡(A)A^{\prime}\subset\mathrm{Frac}(A) be its normalization, i.e. its integral closure in its field of fraction Frac⁡(A)\mathrm{Frac}(A). By results of Seidenberg and Vasconcelos (see e.g. [13, Proposition 1.2.15 and Proposition 1.3.37]), there exists a unique extension of ∂\partial to a locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂′\partial^{\prime} of A′A^{\prime}.

With the above notation, the Rees algebra R(A′,∂′)R(A^{\prime},\partial^{\prime}) is the normalization of the Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial). Then hm∈Fm​d′∖Fm​d−1′h^{m}\in F_{md}^{\prime}\setminus F_{md-1}^{\prime} but on the other hand ∑i=0m−1b(m−i)​n​hi∈Fd​m−1′\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}b_{(m-i)n}h^{i}\in F^{\prime}_{dm-1} as F(m−i)​n+d​i′=Fm​n+(d−n)​i′F^{\prime}_{(m-i)n+di}=F^{\prime}_{mn+(d-n)i} is contained Fd​m−1′F^{\prime}_{dm-1} for every i=0,…,m−1i=0,\ldots,m-1. This is absurd, so h∈Fn′h\in F_{n}^{\prime} and then g∈R′g\in R^{\prime}. ∎

Corollary 19.

Corollary 21.

Let AA be a finitely generated kk-algebra endowed with a nonzero locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial. If R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is a finitely generated kk-algebra, then so is R(A[I/f]),∂′)R(A[I/f]),\partial^{\prime}) for every equivariant affine modification A⁡[I/f]A[I/f] of AA.

2.3. Finitely generated Rees algebras

It is well known that the ring of invariants of a 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on an affine kk-variety X=Spec⁡(A)X=\mathrm{Spec}(A) is in general not finitely generated (see e.g. [15, Chapter 7] for a survey). As a consequence, the Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) as well as the associated graded algebra gr∂​A\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A of an integral kk-algebra of finite type AA endowed with a non-zero locally nilpotent kk-derivation are in general not finitely generated. Our aim in this subsection is to give an algebro-geometric construction of all pairs (A,∂)(A,\partial) consisting of a kk-algebra of finite type and a locally nilpotent kk-derivation of AA for which the Rees algebra (A,∂)(A,\partial) is finitely generated. Since normalization is a finite morphism, it follows from the Artin-Tate lemma that a kk-algebra is finitely generated if and only its normalization is finitely generated. By Lemma 18, we can thus restrict without loss of generality to the case of normal kk-algebras.

Lemma 22.

Let (A,∂)(A,\partial) be an integral normal kk-algebra of finite type endowed with a locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial, let {Fn}n≥0\{F_{n}\}_{n\geq 0} be the associated ascending filtration and let R(A,∂)=⨁n≥0FnR(A,\partial)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}F_{n} be its Rees algebra. Then the following are equivalent:

1) The algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is finitely generated over kk,

2) The associated graded algebra gr∂​A\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A is finitely generated over kk,

3) The kk-algebra A0=F0=ker∂A_{0}=F_{0}=\mathrm{ker}\partial is finitely generated and R(A,∂)+=⨁n>0FnR(A,\partial)_{+}=\bigoplus_{n>0}F_{n} is a finitely generated R(A,∂)R(A,\partial)-module.

To show the implication 2) ⇒\Rightarrow 3), we can assume without loss of generality that gr∂​A=k⁡[b1,…,br]\mathrm{gr}_{\partial}A=k[b_{1},\ldots,b_{r}] for some nonzero homogeneous elements bi∈Fd⁡(i)/Fd⁡(i)−1b_{i}\in F_{d(i)}/F_{d(i)-1}, i=1,…,ri=1,\ldots,r, where d⁡(i)=0d(i)=0 for i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,m and d⁡(i)>0d(i)>0 for i=m+1,…,ri=m+1,\ldots,r. It follows in particular that F0=F0/F−1F_{0}=F_{0}/F_{-1} is generated by b1,…,bmb_{1},\ldots,b_{m}. Choosing representatives ai∈Fd⁡(i)∖Fd⁡(i)−1a_{i}\in F_{d(i)}\setminus F_{d(i)-1} of the classes bib_{i}, we have F0=k⁡[b1,…,bm]=k⁡[a1,…,am]F_{0}=k[b_{1},\ldots,b_{m}]=k[a_{1},\ldots,a_{m}]. We claim that R(A,∂)+R(A,\partial)_{+} is equal to the homogeneous ideal II generated by θ\theta and the elements ai​θd⁡(i)a_{i}\theta^{d(i)}, i=m+1,…,ri=m+1,\ldots,r. Indeed, let fθd∈Fdθd⊂R(A,∂)+f\theta^{d}\in F_{d}\theta^{d}\subset R(A,\partial)_{+} be a homogeneous element and let d0d_{0} be minimal such that f∈Fd0∖Fd0−1f\in F_{d_{0}}\setminus F_{d_{0}-1}. If d0<dd_{0}<d then fθd0∈Fd0θd0⊂R(A,∂)f\theta^{d_{0}}\in F_{d_{0}}\theta^{d_{0}}\subset R(A,\partial) and then f​θd=(f​θd0)​θd−d0∈If\theta^{d}=(f\theta^{d_{0}})\theta^{d-d_{0}}\in I. Otherwise, if d0=dd_{0}=d, the residue class f¯\overline{f} of ff in Fd/Fd−1F_{d}/F_{d-1} is nonzero, and by hypothesis, there exists a homogeneous polynomial P∈F0​[tm+1,…,tr]P\in F_{0}[t_{m+1},\ldots,t_{r}] of degree dd with respect to the weights d⁡(ti)=d⁡(i)d(t_{i})=d(i), i=m+1,…,ri=m+1,\ldots,r, such that f¯=P⁡(bm+1,…,br)\overline{f}=P(b_{m+1},\ldots,b_{r}). It follows that

is contained in the subspace Fd−1​θdF_{d-1}\theta^{d}, hence is equal to (gd−1​θd−1)​θ(g_{d-1}\theta^{d-1})\theta for some element gd−1​θd−1∈Fd−1​θd−1g_{d-1}\theta^{d-1}\in F_{d-1}\theta^{d-1} of R(A,∂)R(A,\partial), which implies in turn that f​θdf\theta^{d} belongs to II. ∎

2.3.1. Geometric criterion for finite generation

Recall that a ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-fibration between algebraic kk-varieties is a surjective projective morphism of finite type π:Y→Y0\pi:Y\rightarrow Y_{0} whose fiber YηY_{\eta} over the generic point η\eta of Y0Y_{0} is isomorphic to the projective line ℙk⁡(Y0)1\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1} over the field of rational functions k⁡(Y0)k(Y_{0}) of Y0Y_{0}.

Proposition 23.

Let (A,∂)(A,\partial) be an integral normal kk-algebra of finite type endowed with a nontrivial locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial whose Rees algebra R(A,∂)=⨁n≥0Fnθn⊆A[θ]R(A,\partial)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}F_{n}\theta^{n}\subseteq A[\theta] is a finitely generated kk-algebra. Let A0=F0A_{0}=F_{0} and let

X=Spec(A)↪Y=Projk(R(A,∂))X=\mathrm{Spec}(A)\hookrightarrow Y=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(A,\partial))

be the open embedding of schemes over Y0=Spec⁡(A0)Y_{0}=\mathrm{Spec}(A_{0}) induced by the graded inclusion η:R(A,∂)↪A[θ]\eta:R(A,\partial)\hookrightarrow A[\theta] ((see (1.2))). Then the following hold:

1) The schemes Y0Y_{0} and YY are normal kk-varieties,

2) The structure morphism π:Y→Y0\pi:Y\rightarrow Y_{0} is a ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-fibration,

3) The effective Weil divisor B=V+​(θ)B=V_{+}(\theta) on YY is ample and the restriction of the sheaf 𝒪Y​(B)\mathcal{O}_{Y}(B) to the generic fiber Yη≅ℙk⁡(Y0)1Y_{\eta}\cong\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1} of π\pi is equal to 𝒪ℙk⁡(Y0)1​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1}}(1).

Proof.

By Lemma 22, A0A_{0} is a kk-algebra of finite type. Since AA is normal by assumption, the normality of Y0=Spec⁡(A0)Y_{0}=\mathrm{Spec}(A_{0}) and YY follow from [15, Proposition 1.13] and Lemma 18 respectively. Since R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is finitely generated over A0A_{0}, it follows from [16, Proposition 4.6.18] that π:Y=Projk(R(A,∂))→Y0\pi:Y=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(A,\partial))\rightarrow Y_{0} is a morphism of finite type and that there exists d≥1d\geq 1 such that the quasi-coherent 𝒪Y\mathcal{O}_{Y}-module 𝒪Y​(d)\mathcal{O}_{Y}(d) associated to FdF_{d} is invertible and π\pi-ample. It follows that d​B=V+​(θd)dB=V_{+}(\theta^{d}) is a π\pi-ample Cartier divisor, and since Y0Y_{0} is affine, we deduce in turn from [16, Proposition 4.5.10] that BB is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-Cartier and ample on YY. By Lemma 6, the image of the open embedding X↪YX\hookrightarrow Y coincides with the complement of the support of BB on YY. Furthermore, by Lemma 8, the inclusion X↪YX\hookrightarrow Y is equivariant for the 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions associated with the locally nilpotent kk-derivations ∂\partial and θ​R​(∂)\theta R(\partial) on AA and R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) respectively. Lemma 16 implies that for every s∈F1∖F0s\in F_{1}\setminus F_{0}, we have an isomophism

(R(A,∂)∂s,θR(∂))≅((A0)∂s[s,θ],θ∂∂s).(R(A,\partial)_{\partial s},\theta R(\partial))\cong((A_{0})_{\partial s}[s,\theta],\theta\tfrac{\partial}{\partial s}).

It follows that the restriction of π\pi over the principal affine open subset (Y0)∂s≅Spec⁡((A0)∂s)(Y_{0})_{\partial s}\cong\mathrm{Spec}((A_{0})_{\partial s}) is isomorphic to the trivial ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-bundle Projk​((A0)∂s​[s,θ])→(Y0)∂s\mathrm{Proj}_{k}((A_{0})_{\partial s}[s,\theta])\rightarrow(Y_{0})_{\partial s} and that the restriction of 𝒪Y​(B)\mathcal{O}_{Y}(B) over (Y0)∂s(Y_{0})_{\partial s} is equal to 𝒪ℙ(A0)∂s1​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}_{(A_{0})_{\partial s}}^{1}}(1). ∎

Conversely, given a normal affine kk-variety Y0Y_{0} and a ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-fibration π:Y→Y0\pi:Y\rightarrow Y_{0} where YY is a normal kk-variety, it is a natural question to characterize which effective Weil divisors BB on YY have the property that their complements are affine varieties carrying 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions with finitely generated associated Rees algebras. Recall that a Weil divisor BB on a kk-variety YY is called semi-ample if there exists n≥1n\geq 1 such that the sheaf 𝒪Y​(n​B)\mathcal{O}_{Y}(nB) is invertible and generated by its global sections. We then have the following criterion:

Theorem 24.

Let Y0=Spec⁡(A0)Y_{0}=\mathrm{Spec}(A_{0}) be a normal affine kk-variety and let π:Y→Y0\pi:Y\rightarrow Y_{0} be a ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-fibration where YY is a normal kk-variety. Let BB an effective semi-ample Weil divisor on YY with the following properties:

a) The scheme X=Y∖BX=Y\setminus B is an affine kk-variety,

b) The restriction of the sheaf 𝒪Y​(B)\mathcal{O}_{Y}(B) to the generic fiber Yη≅ℙk⁡(Y0)1Y_{\eta}\cong\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1} of π\pi is equal to 𝒪ℙk⁡(Y0)1​(1)\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1}}(1).

Then the following hold:

1) There exists a nontrivial 𝔾a,Y0\mathbb{G}_{a,Y_{0}}-action on YY which leaves BB invariant and restricts to a 𝔾a,Y0\mathbb{G}_{a,Y_{0}}-action on XX.

2) The Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) of the locally nilpotent kk-derivation ∂\partial of A=Γ⁡(X,𝒪X)A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal{O}_{X}) corresponding to the induced 𝔾a,Y0\mathbb{G}_{a,Y_{0}}-action on XX is a finitely generated A0A_{0}-algebra isomorphic to R⁡(Y,B)=⨁n≥0H0​(Y,𝒪Y​(n​B))R(Y,B)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y}(nB)).

Proof.

By definition, ℒ=𝒪Y​(B)\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{O}_{Y}(B) is the reflexive subsheaf of rank 11 of the constant sheaf 𝒦Y\mathcal{K}_{Y} of rational functions on YY defined by

ℒ(U)={f∈𝒦Y(U),div(f)+B|U≥0}∪{0}\mathcal{L}(U)=\{f\in\mathcal{K}_{Y}(U),\mathrm{div}(f)+B|_{U}\geq 0\}\cup\{0\}

for every open subset UU of YY. The fact that BB is effective implies that the constant section 11 of 𝒦Y\mathcal{K}_{Y} is contained in ℒ\mathcal{L}. We denote by θ∈H0​(Y,ℒ)\theta\in H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}) the corresponding global section of ℒ\mathcal{L} whose zero locus is equal to BB. We then get an inclusion

H0​(Y,𝒪Y)↪H0​(Y,ℒ),f↦f​θ.H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y})\hookrightarrow H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}),\;f\mapsto f\theta.

Since YY is projective over the affine variety Y0Y_{0}, by [17, Chapter III,Theorem 5.2], we have H0​(Y,𝒪Y)=A0H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{O}_{Y})=A_{0} and H0​(Y,ℒ⊗n)H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) is a finitely generated A0A_{0}-module for every nn. Furthermore, the restriction homomorphism

H0​(Y,ℒ⊗n)→H0​(Yη,ℒ⊗n)=H0​(Yη,𝒪Yη​(n​B|Yη))≅H0​(ℙk⁡(Y0)1,𝒪ℙk⁡(Y0)1​(n))H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})\rightarrow H^{0}(Y_{\eta},\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})=H^{0}(Y_{\eta},\mathcal{O}_{Y_{\eta}}(nB|_{Y_{\eta}}))\cong H^{0}(\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1},\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}_{k(Y_{0})}^{1}}(n))

is surjective. The fact that for an effective semi-ample Weil divisor BB the algebra R⁡(Y,ℒ)=R⁡(Y,B)R(Y,\mathcal{L})=R(Y,B) is finitely generated over A0A_{0} is a classical result due to Zariski (see e.g. [31]). Let us briefly recall the argument. Since ℒ\mathcal{L} is semi-ample, it follows from [24, Theorem 2.1.27] that for sufficiently big and divisible d≥1d\geq 1, the sheaf ℒ⊗d\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d} is invertible and the rational map

ψd:Y⇢ℙ⁡(H0​(Y,ℒ⊗d)∗)\psi_{d}:Y\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}(H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d})^{*})

is an everywhere defined morphism of Y0Y_{0}-schemes with connected fibers, whose image is a normal variety πd:Yd→Y0\pi_{d}:Y_{d}\rightarrow Y_{0} projective over Y0Y_{0}, and such that we have ℒ⊗d=ψd∗​𝒪Yd​(1)\mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}=\psi_{d}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{Y_{d}}(1). This implies that the Veronese subring R​(Y,ℒ)(d)=⨁n≥0H0​(Y,ℒ⊗n​d)R(Y,\mathcal{L})^{(d)}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes nd}) is finitely generated over A0A_{0}, and hence that R⁡(Y,B)=R⁡(Y,ℒ)R(Y,B)=R(Y,\mathcal{L}) is finitely generated by [3, Corollary 1.2.5].

It follows that Y′=Projk​(R⁡(Y,B))Y^{\prime}=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(Y,B)) is a normal variety, projective over Y0Y_{0} and that the canonical rational map of Y0Y_{0}-schemes

ψ:Y⇢Y′=Projk​(R⁡(Y,B))\psi:Y\dashrightarrow Y^{\prime}=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(Y,B))

is a morphism. Since by hypothesis the restriction of ℒ\mathcal{L} to YηY_{\eta} is invertible and very ample, ψ\psi restricts to an isomorphism over the generic point η\eta of Y0Y_{0}, hence is birational. Furthermore, since X=Y∖BX=Y\setminus B is affine hence does not contain any complete curve, it follows that B⋅C>0B\cdot C>0 for every complete curve in YY intersecting XX. This implies that the restriction of ψ\psi to Y∖BY\setminus B is quasi-finite and birational, hence an isomorphism onto its image by Zariski Main Theorem. The latter coincides by construction with the complement

D+​(θ)≅Spec⁡(R⁡(Y,B)/(1−θ)​R​(Y,B))D_{+}(\theta)\cong\mathrm{Spec}(R(Y,B)/(1-\theta)R(Y,B))

of the Weil divisor B′=V+​(θ)B^{\prime}=V_{+}(\theta) on Y′Y^{\prime}. Hypothesis b) implies further that there exists a global section s∈H0​(Y,ℒ)s\in H^{0}(Y,\mathcal{L}) different from θ\theta such that

Projk​(R⁡(Y,B))×Y0Spec⁡(k⁡(Y0))≅Projk⁡(Y0)​(k⁡(Y0)​[s,θ]).\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(Y,B))\times_{Y_{0}}\mathrm{Spec}(k(Y_{0}))\cong\mathrm{Proj}_{k(Y_{0})}(k(Y_{0})[s,\theta]).

It follows that there exists f∈A0f\in A_{0} such that the homogeneous locally nilpotent k⁡(Y0)k(Y_{0})-derivation f​θ​∂∂sf\theta\frac{\partial}{\partial s} of degree 00 of k​(Y0)​[s,θ]k(Y_{0})[s,\theta] extends to a homogeneous locally nilpotent A0A_{0}-derivation ∂~\tilde{\partial} of R⁡(Y,B)R(Y,B) of degree 00 defining a 𝔾a,Y0\mathbb{G}_{a,Y_{0}}-action on Y′Y^{\prime} leaving the Weil divisor B′B^{\prime} invariant and inducing the trivial action on B′B^{\prime}. Since ψ:Y→Y′\psi:Y\rightarrow Y^{\prime} restricts to an isomorphism Y∖B→Y′∖B′Y\setminus B\rightarrow Y^{\prime}\setminus B^{\prime}, this action lifts to a 𝔾a,Y0\mathbb{G}_{a,Y_{0}}-action on YY leaving BB invariant and hence X=Y∖BX=Y\setminus B invariant. By construction, the Rees algebra of the associated locally nilpotent A0A_{0}-derivation ∂\partial of Γ⁡(X,𝒪X)\Gamma(X,\mathcal{O}_{X}) is isomorphic to the finitely generated algebra R⁡(Y,B)=R⁡(Y′,B′)R(Y,B)=R(Y^{\prime},B^{\prime}). ∎

Given a pair (π:Y→Y0,B)(\pi:Y\rightarrow Y_{0},B) satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 24, the proof actually shows that the composition of the open embedding X=Y∖B↪YX=Y\setminus B\hookrightarrow Y with the canonical morphism

ψ:Y→Y′=Projk​(R⁡(Y,B))\psi:Y\rightarrow Y^{\prime}=\mathrm{Proj}_{k}(R(Y,B))

of schemes over Y0Y_{0} is an open embedding of XX in Y′Y^{\prime} as the complement of the ample Weil divisor B′=ψ∗​(B)B^{\prime}=\psi_{*}(B). The following example illustrates the fact that even when XX is smooth, the variety Y′Y^{\prime} can have bad singularities supported along B′B^{\prime} so that, depending on the context, it can be more convenient to consider a model (Y,B)(Y,B) with better singularities but non-ample boundary divisor BB.

Example 25.

Let X⊂𝔸k4=Spec⁡(k⁡[x,y,u,v])X\subset\mathbb{A}_{k}^{4}=\mathrm{Spec}(k[x,y,u,v]) be the smooth affine 33-fold with equation x​v=y⁡(y​u+1)xv=y(yu+1). The locally nilpotent k⁡[x,y]k[x,y]-derivation

∂=x​∂∂u+y2​∂∂v\partial=x\tfrac{\partial}{\partial u}+y^{2}\tfrac{\partial}{\partial v}

of the coordinate ring AA of XX defines a 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on XX. 3. Examples and Applications

In this section, we first illustrate the computation and geometric properties of Rees algebras on a series of classical examples in the study of additive group actions on affine varieties, with a particular focus on the interplay between the relative and absolute Rees algebras and the construction of vector bundles of rank two on certain geometric quotients. We then consider an application of Rees algebras to the construction of families of affine extensions of 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-torsors over punctured smooth surfaces.

3.1. Danielewski hypersurfaces in 𝔸k3\mathbb{A}_{k}^{3}

For every nonzero polynomial q⁡(x)∈k⁡[x]q(x)\in k[x], the surface Sn,PS_{n,P} is equipped with a nontrivial 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action μ\mu associated to the locally nilpotent k⁡[x]k[x]-derivation

3.2. A smooth affine threefold whose geometric quotient is quasi-projective but not quasi-affine

It is known in general that the geometric quotient X/𝔾aX/\mathbb{G}_{a} of a proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on a factorial affine variety is a quasi-affine variety (see e.g. [5]). For smooth affine threefolds XX, factorial or not, it is a consequence of Chow’s Lemma that the algebraic space geometric quotient X/𝔾aX/\mathbb{G}_{a} of a proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action is a quasi-projective surface. In this subsection, we consider a simple example of a smooth non-factorial affine threefold XX endowed with a proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action, whose geometric quotient is a smooth quasi-projective surface which is not quasi-affine.

3.4. Winkelmann’s proper locally trivial action on 𝔸k5\mathbb{A}_{k}^{5}

A 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on an affine space 𝔸kn\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n} is called a translation if its geometric quotient 𝔸kn/𝔾a\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n}/\mathbb{G}_{a} is isomorphic to 𝔸kn−1\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n-1} and 𝔸kn\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n} is equivariantly isomorphic to (𝔸kn/𝔾a)×𝔾a(\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n}/\mathbb{G}_{a})\times\mathbb{G}_{a} on which 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} acts by translations on the second factor. It is classical that proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions on 𝔸k2\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2} and 𝔸k3\mathbb{A}_{k}^{3} are translations. The question whether a proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on 𝔸k4\mathbb{A}_{k}^{4} is a translation is still widely open (see e.g. [10, 20] for partial results). Examples of proper 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions on affine spaces 𝔸kn\mathbb{A}_{k}^{n}, n≥5n\geq 5, which fail to be translations were constructed by Winkelmann [30]. We consider the simplest of these examples, in dimension 55.

Let A=k​[u,v]​[x,y,z]A=k[u,v][x,y,z] and let μ\mu be the fixed point free 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-action on 𝔸k5=Spec⁡(A)\mathbb{A}_{k}^{5}=\mathrm{Spec}(A) determined by the triangular locally nilpotent k⁡[u,v]k[u,v]-derivation

∂=u​∂∂x+v​∂∂y+(1+w)​∂∂z,\partial=u\tfrac{\partial}{\partial x}+v\tfrac{\partial}{\partial y}+(1+w)\tfrac{\partial}{\partial z},

where w=x​v−y​uw=xv-yu.

The Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is isomorphic to the quotient of the polynomial ring A⁡[w,c1,c2,θ]A[w,c_{1},c_{2},\theta] endowed with the grading defined by the weights ωu=ωv=ωw=ωc1=ωc2=0\omega_{u}=\omega_{v}=\omega_{w}=\omega_{c_{1}}=\omega_{c_{2}}=0, ωx=ωy=ωz=ωθ=1\omega_{x}=\omega_{y}=\omega_{z}=\omega_{\theta}=1 by the homogeneous ideal II generated by the polynomials v​c1−u​c2−w⁡(w+1)vc_{1}-uc_{2}-w(w+1), c2​x−c1​y+w​zc_{2}x-c_{1}y+wz, w​θ+u​y−v​xw\theta+uy-vx, c2​θ+v​z−(1+w)​yc_{2}\theta+vz-(1+w)y and c1​θ+u​z−(1+w)​xc_{1}\theta+uz-(1+w)x.

By [30], the kernel A0=F0A_{0}=F_{0} of ∂\partial is generated by uu, vv, w=x​v−y​uw=xv-yu, c1=x⁡(1+w)−u​zc_{1}=x(1+w)-uz and c2=y⁡(1+w)−v​zc_{2}=y(1+w)-vz, with the unique relation v​c1−u​c2−w⁡(1+w)=0vc_{1}-uc_{2}-w(1+w)=0. Furthermore, since we have

the Rees algebra R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is generated over A0A_{0} by xx, yy, zz and θ\theta. These elements of AA satisfy the linear dependence relations c1​θ+u​z−(1+w)​x=0c_{1}\theta+uz-(1+w)x=0, c2​θ+v​z−(1+w)​y=0c_{2}\theta+vz-(1+w)y=0 and w​θ+u​y−v​x=0w\theta+uy-vx=0 over A0A_{0}. Furthermore, the element c2​x−c1​y+w​z∈F1c_{2}x-c_{1}y+wz\in F_{1} belongs to F0F_{0}, which yields the additional relation c2​x−c1​y+w​z=0⋅θ=0c_{2}x-c_{1}y+wz=0\cdot\theta=0. It follows that R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is a quotient of the ring B=k⁡[u,v,w,c1,c2]​[x,y,z,θ]/IB=k[u,v,w,c_{1},c_{2}][x,y,z,\theta]/I. The images of ww and (1+w)(1+w) generate the unit ideal in BB, and the localizations B(1+w)≅A0​[(1+w)−1]​[z,θ]B_{(1+w)}\cong A_{0}[(1+w)^{-1}][z,\theta] and Bw≅A0​[w−1]​[x,y]B_{w}\cong A_{0}[w^{-1}][x,y] are integral domains of dimension 66. The homomorphism B→Bw×B(1+w)B\rightarrow B_{w}\times B_{(1+w)} is thus injective, which implies in turn that BB is an integral domain of dimension 66. Since R(A,∂)R(A,\partial) is itself an integral domain of dimension 66 as AA is of dimension 55, we conclude that R(A,∂)=BR(A,\partial)=B. ∎

The image of the algebraic quotient morphism π:𝔸k5→Q=Spec⁡(A0)\pi:\mathbb{A}_{k}^{5}\rightarrow Q=\mathrm{Spec}(A_{0}) is equal to the complement of the codimension 22 closed subset W={u=v=1+w=0}≅Spec(k[c1,c2])W=\{u=v=1+w=0\}\cong\mathrm{Spec}(k[c_{1},c_{2}]) in the smooth affine quadric

It follows from the proof of Lemma 30 that the morphism p¯:Y=Spec(R(A,∂))→Q\overline{p}:Y=\mathrm{Spec}(R(A,\partial))\rightarrow Q induced by the inclusion A0=Γ(Q,𝒪Q)⊂R(A,∂)A_{0}=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal{O}_{Q})\subset R(A,\partial) is vector bundle of rank 22, which becomes trivial on the cover of QQ by the the principal affine open subsets QwQ_{w} and Q(1+w)Q_{(1+w)}, and whose restriction over S=Q∖WS=Q\setminus W coincides with the vector bundle p:V=SpecS​(Sym⋅​ℱ1)→Sp:V=\mathrm{Spec}_{S}(\mathrm{Sym}^{\cdot}\mathcal{F}_{1})\rightarrow S.

Lemma 31.

The vector bundles p¯:Y=Spec(R(A,∂))→Q\overline{p}:Y=\mathrm{Spec}(R(A,\partial))\rightarrow Q and p:V=SpecS​(Sym⋅​ℱ1)→Sp:V=\mathrm{Spec}_{S}(\mathrm{Sym}^{\cdot}\mathcal{F}_{1})\rightarrow S are nontrivial.

Proof.

The homomorphism A0​[x,y,z,θ]→A0A_{0}[x,y,z,\theta]\rightarrow A_{0}, (x,y,z,θ)↦(u,v,(1+w),0)(x,y,z,\theta)\mapsto(u,v,(1+w),0) induces a homomorphism R(A,∂)→A0R(A,\partial)\rightarrow A_{0} defining a section s:Q→Ys:Q\rightarrow Y of p¯:Y→Q\overline{p}:Y\rightarrow Q whose zero locus is equal to the closed variety WW. It follows that π−1​(o)\pi^{-1}(o) is not empty, hence that j:P↪Xj:P\hookrightarrow X is a normal affine extension of PP with finitely generated Rees BB-algebra R(A,∂X)≅RXR(A,\partial_{X})\cong R_{X}. ∎

Example 34.
